hero.headline: Byron Donalds raises $90 million for Governor's race as opponents struggle with fundraising
hero.teaser: U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds consolidated virtually all major Republican endorsements and continues to dominate fundraising in the gubernatorial primary, raising nearly $2 million in one week alone.
hero.body:
Byron Donalds' campaign reported raising $90 million for his gubernatorial bid, with Division of Elections records showing nearly $10 million in contributions to his campaign account and more than $76.2 million to the Friends of Byron Donalds political committee through June 26. The campaign raised nearly $2 million between June 20 and June 26. Contributors donating at least $250,000 during that week included GOPAC Election Fund, Ferreira Construction of New Jersey, Phillips Infrastructure of Tennessee, and the Southern Group. The campaign recently launched a $20 million statewide ad buy on television and digital platforms.

Donalds secured endorsements in the past week from U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody, Attorney General James Uthmeier, Agriculture Secretary Wilton Simpson, CFO Blaise Ingoglia, incoming Florida Senate President Jim Boyd, and Florida House Speaker-designate Sam Garrison. His opponents face significant fundraising gaps ahead of the August 18 Primary. Lt. Gov. Jay Collins raised nearly $15,500 in hard money and just $100 to his Quiet Professionals FL political committee during the same week, with less than $3.5 million as of June 26.

Collins has not responded to charges from Gov. Ron DeSantis senior advisors that his wife Layla Collins, who the Governor appointed to the state Board of Education, had burner accounts on X criticizing DeSantis for not boosting his appointed Lieutenant Governor's campaign. The controversy is likely to cast a shadow over both the final stretch of the campaign and the final six months of DeSantis' term.

Collins struggled during a Friday night debate with former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner and investment manager James Fishback. He had difficulty answering questions on issues ranging from data centers to whether he voted for DeSantis in 2018, which he could not do because he was not a Florida resident at the time. Collins also needed notes to help with responses and lost his temper at various points during the debate.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor's wife of running anonymous accounts attacking Governor
cards.teaser: Current and former communications officials from Gov.
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts were deactivated after allegations surfaced that they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins. Christina Pushaw, a Communications Specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, both pointed to online research tying the accounts to the Second Lady. Pushaw shared information posted by Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email similar to ones known to be used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication, which showed an access attempt triggered a message to an email address with letters starred out and to a phone number with only the last digits showing. Pushaw wrote that Layla Collins was appointed to a state board by the same governor she was calling a coward. Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, which she said appeared tied to Layla Collins as well.

Pushaw said the account content was entirely comprised of two types of posts: promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who didn't endorse Jay, including the governor. Redfern posted that the FSUDude account was tied directly to her personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after Pushaw and Redfern leveled their criticisms publicly. Florida Politics requested comment from Jay and Layla Collins. Pushaw and Redfern have both previously served as Press Secretary for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds for Governor. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year.

cards.headline: 40-year-old driver killed in head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
cards.body:
A 40-year-old man was killed early Sunday after a head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened around 2 a.m. near State Road 710, also known as Beeline Highway, and Southwest Silver Fox Lane.

FHP said a 2015 Kia Optima was traveling north on State Road 710 when the driver crossed into the southbound lane and collided head-on with a 2021 Toyota Tundra. The front left of the Kia struck the front left of the Tundra. Upon impact, the Kia burst into flames and came to rest on the grass shoulder facing north. The Tundra came to rest facing southeast in the southbound lane. The driver of the Kia, a 40-year-old man, died at the scene. The driver of the Tundra, a 41-year-old man from Indiantown, was taken to the hospital via LifeStar medical helicopter.

Martin County Fire Rescue has responded to 42 vehicle accident-related calls on State Road 710 just this year. After a fatal crash in January, Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek called the road a "death trap." Bill Townsend, who lives nearby, said the road has long been a concern for residents. "People don't pay a whole lot of attention to other people on the road, and [it's] kind of a dangerous road sometimes," Townsend said. "Everybody's always in a hurry… just living here makes me worry about the young people learning to drive and learning to drive on that road concerns me, because I have young kids."

The Florida Department of Transportation has plans to widen the road from two lanes to four, but construction is not expected to begin until 2031. "The question will be how many more people have to die before we get that project going. Florida touts that they have the safest roads in the country but this road is one that clearly is not in that category," Budensiek said in January. In the meantime, FDOT has begun improvements to the road, including pavement, markings, signage and new turn lanes. Townsend said faster action is needed. "It would be beneficial to the people that live and travel that road all the time if something happened faster," Townsend said.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Florida students reach milestone with 60% testing at grade level in reading and math
cards.teaser: For the first time in state history, 60% of Florida students tested at or above grade level in both reading and math on annual assessments, representing a significant increase from three years ago.
cards.body:
Florida students tested at or above grade level in both reading and math at a 60% rate on the annual Florida Assessment of Student Thinking (FAST) exam, marking the first time in state history the milestone has been reached. Just three years ago, roughly half of Florida students read at grade level. This year's results represent a meaningful climb, though legitimate questions remain about what is driving the improvement.

The results coincided with school grade distributions moving upward across the state. This year, 76% of Florida's 3,428 graded public schools earned an A or B, up from 71% a year ago. The share of schools earning A grades jumped from 44% to 51%. The results were announced as an honorable mention in a winners and losers analysis.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board challenges judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook post
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009 who was suspended last year for Facebook comments about conservative activist Charlie Kirk. In the filing, the school board argued that "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence" and the board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" that made his removal appropriate. Theobald's comments labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report obtained by WPTV, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board still has the final say on whether Theobald gets his job back, though it's unclear when a final decision will be made.

cards.headline: Martin County woman dies in Hobe Sound home fire, community raises funds for fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many belongings.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, said she received a call from White's fiancé Mark stating that Misty had passed away in a fire. Fenn returned to the scene in the days following the tragedy to process her grief and described the home as completely in a state of devastation.

Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn said the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured, as he lost his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. Fenn reflected on her friendship with White and said she was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants and playing the piano. White was always the first to lend a hand and loved kids and people. The timing of White's death adds another layer of heartbreak for those who knew her. White's birthday is the Fourth of July, and she passed just a few days before her birthday.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year as inflation hits holiday staples
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation.
cards.body:
The Fourth of July means cookouts, grilling and picnics, and this year, that tradition comes with a higher price tag. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points squarely at inflation, with ground beef up 5.5%, buns up 7.7%, strawberries up 12.4% after a Florida frost, and ice cream up 5.3%.

Not everything is more expensive this year. Potato prices are down, which is good news for potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal.

Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch said there are ways to keep costs in check. It's really important to shop savvier than ever by comparing stores to see who has the best deals for the groceries on your list, Woroch said. The biggest thing for families is cutting down the food waste, and that begins with a meal plan.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie City Council to vote on giving 7 acres to FDOT for Midway Road Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange at Midway Road and Florida's Turnpike. Final approval is scheduled for an upcoming meeting.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with the interchange. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange is about accessibility and keeping up with growth in the city. Samples said the project will accommodate the growth that has already occurred and the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website for the project, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase and construction is anticipated to begin in Summer 2027.

FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange for the Turnpike. According to the FDOT website, the partial interchange is still in the design phase. Erin Scheumeister, a Port St. Lucie resident, said the construction can be annoying but believes it is necessary. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Peacock House Art Foundation offers tours, art classes in historic Crain Estate
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation in Fort Pierce preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain in the historic Crain Estate. The foundation offers guided tours and an artist-in-residency program attracting artists from around the world.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation operates out of the historic Crain Estate in Fort Pierce, preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain who once lived there. The property was a private residence before becoming a non-profit organization that now puts the Peacock Arts District on the map and connects local and international artists. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the entire facility from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Many parts of the house remain the same as when the Crains lived there, including the smoking and bourbon room with man paneling, manly bathroom colors, and stained glass. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India that features tiny peacocks. The foundation keeps the estate 90% the way it was when the Crains were here.

The property gets its name from peacocks that have roamed there for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, bringing in seven originally. From those seven, there are now over 100 birds on the property. Among the flock is a beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old and recognizable because he walks with a limp. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world, housing them in simple but elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, including private one-on-one sessions, sculpting, and watercolor workshops.

cards.headline: Stuart breast cancer patient speaks out after Anthem Blue Cross denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, had her insurance deny coverage for breast reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before it was scheduled. The denial involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex that Anthem considers investigational.
cards.body:
Three months ago, Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. Her treatment plan was a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Clark had the mastectomy, but less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery, which involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, is still considered investigational and there is no or not enough proof it improves health. GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh that has become a controversial treatment for breast reconstruction. While it is popular among plastic surgeons and approved by the FDA for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and is still considered an off-label, investigational, and experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA reiterated that its efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined.

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product is giving her patients the least amount of complications. Despite her insurer's denial, Clark got her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago, thanks to Billington. Last year, after investigative reporting shared breast cancer patients' stories of denial, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. A spokesperson with Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield said the company regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence and aligned with the latest treatment standards and expert recommendations, adding that without FDA approval, the mesh does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by its medical policy.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue 2 boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1. Both occupants were wearing life jackets and were rescued without injury.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from marine deputies and the life-saving decision to wear life jackets. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded.

Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. The sheriff's office said in a Facebook post that this incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life and that they are grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call.

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock closes today for $3 million renovation, capacity to nearly double
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock closed July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The year-long project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees and will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually. Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. Boat captain Parker Fisher, who is based in Stuart, said the dock has needed work over the years and he is glad the city is putting money into it.

During the closure, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters who rely on the dock for drop-off and pick-up. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, initially had concerns about whether it could continue running during construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city is allowing the company to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock's non-floating section for boarding passengers. Kuyrkendall said Stuart is not Stuart without the water. He said weekends can get hectic at the dock with boats squeezing in and trying to find spots, and that modernizing and expanding the dock will be great for the city and for Tiki Taxi & Cruises.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury. The 44-year-old Serena was injured during her singles return earlier in the week in a three-set loss. She posted on Instagram that she is heartbroken to have to withdraw from doubles and that coming back to compete again has been a gift. Serena said the opportunity to play alongside Venus once more meant the world to her and that she did everything she could but her knee is not ready to compete. The post included images of four syringes that Serena said shows the fluid drained from her knee after her singles match. An accompanying video showed her walking with strapping up and down her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her.

Serena was beaten 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 by 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday. Venus, who is 46, played in the mixed doubles tournament on Friday together with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool. The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in the only first-round doubles match that was not scheduled earlier in the week, having been pushed back to give Serena more time to recover. With the U.S. Open approaching, Serena indicated she could play again somewhere else soon, saying all she can say is stay tuned to a city near you. The Williams sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon.

cards.headline: Argentina survives Cape Verde 3-2 in World Cup thriller
cards.teaser: Defending World Cup champion Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday in South Florida, advancing to the Round of 16 after the tiny island nation challenged them until the final minutes of extra time.
cards.body:
The go-ahead score for Argentina was credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute. Lionel Messi scored early in regulation, his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal. Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1.

Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored for Cape Verde, both equalizers that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida. Cape Verde's 40-year-old goalkeeper Vozinha had 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi. Cape Verde became the smallest country to reach the knockout round, securing surprising draws against Spain, Uruguay and Saudi Arabia.

Messi sneaked behind the Cape Verde defense on a well-timed run as Martinez lofted a pass toward him, taking a quick touch and hammering a finish into the roof of the net past Vozinha for a 1-0 lead in the 29th minute. Messi now has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbappe in the Golden Boot race, and extended his World Cup record to 12 goals during his record eight-match scoring streak. Argentina advanced to face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is preparing for the 2026 fall season with state title aspirations after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district championship. A second-round playoff exit left the team feeling like more was within reach. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson said most of the seniors are four-year seniors, with the majority coming from the middle school program. Robertson said the seniors know how things are run and have had success in their careers, and he hopes their senior year will be the best season the program has had.

The veteran senior class is leading the program into a more demanding schedule this fall. Senior Jack Williams said the team wanted to take the program to the next level with a challenging schedule by playing against really good teams and attracting new people. Senior Jack Whelche said a better year means going farther in the playoffs, noting that going undefeated in the regular season does not matter if they keep losing in the second round. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the daily summer workouts add up as something to look forward to, working harder to see positive results when the season starts and break their record.

Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

hero.headline: Byron Donalds raises $90 million for Governor's race as opponents struggle with fundraising
hero.teaser: U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds consolidated virtually all major Republican endorsements and continues to dominate fundraising in the gubernatorial primary, raising nearly $2 million in one week alone.
hero.body:
Byron Donalds' campaign reported raising $90 million for his gubernatorial bid, with Division of Elections records showing nearly $10 million in contributions to his campaign account and more than $76.2 million to the Friends of Byron Donalds political committee through June 26. The campaign raised nearly $2 million between June 20 and June 26. Contributors donating at least $250,000 during that week included GOPAC Election Fund, Ferreira Construction of New Jersey, Phillips Infrastructure of Tennessee, and the Southern Group. The campaign recently launched a $20 million statewide ad buy on television and digital platforms.

Donalds secured endorsements in the past week from U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody, Attorney General James Uthmeier, Agriculture Secretary Wilton Simpson, CFO Blaise Ingoglia, incoming Florida Senate President Jim Boyd, and Florida House Speaker-designate Sam Garrison. His opponents face significant fundraising gaps ahead of the August 18 Primary. Lt. Gov. Jay Collins raised nearly $15,500 in hard money and just $100 to his Quiet Professionals FL political committee during the same week, with less than $3.5 million as of June 26.

Collins has not responded to charges from Gov. Ron DeSantis senior advisors that his wife Layla Collins, who the Governor appointed to the state Board of Education, had burner accounts on X criticizing DeSantis for not boosting his appointed Lieutenant Governor's campaign. The controversy is likely to cast a shadow over both the final stretch of the campaign and the final six months of DeSantis' term.

Collins struggled during a Friday night debate with former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner and investment manager James Fishback. He had difficulty answering questions on issues ranging from data centers to whether he voted for DeSantis in 2018, which he could not do because he was not a Florida resident at the time. Collins also needed notes to help with responses and lost his temper at various points during the debate.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor's wife of running anonymous accounts attacking Governor
cards.teaser: Current and former communications officials from Gov.
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts were deactivated after allegations surfaced that they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins. Christina Pushaw, a Communications Specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, both pointed to online research tying the accounts to the Second Lady. Pushaw shared information posted by Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email similar to ones known to be used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication, which showed an access attempt triggered a message to an email address with letters starred out and to a phone number with only the last digits showing. Pushaw wrote that Layla Collins was appointed to a state board by the same governor she was calling a coward. Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, which she said appeared tied to Layla Collins as well.

Pushaw said the account content was entirely comprised of two types of posts: promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who didn't endorse Jay, including the governor. Redfern posted that the FSUDude account was tied directly to her personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after Pushaw and Redfern leveled their criticisms publicly. Florida Politics requested comment from Jay and Layla Collins. Pushaw and Redfern have both previously served as Press Secretary for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds for Governor. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year.

cards.headline: Florida students reach milestone with 60% testing at grade level in reading and math
cards.teaser: For the first time in state history, 60% of Florida students tested at or above grade level in both reading and math on annual assessments, representing a significant increase from three years ago.
cards.body:
Florida students tested at or above grade level in both reading and math at a 60% rate on the annual Florida Assessment of Student Thinking (FAST) exam, marking the first time in state history the milestone has been reached. Just three years ago, roughly half of Florida students read at grade level. This year's results represent a meaningful climb, though legitimate questions remain about what is driving the improvement.

The results coincided with school grade distributions moving upward across the state. This year, 76% of Florida's 3,428 graded public schools earned an A or B, up from 71% a year ago. The share of schools earning A grades jumped from 44% to 51%. The results were announced as an honorable mention in a winners and losers analysis.

cards.headline: FEMA awards $7.2 million to four Florida communities for Hurricane Ian recovery projects
cards.teaser: FloridaCommerce announced distribution of federal hazard mitigation funds to Charlotte County, Port of the Islands, Seminole County, and Palatka for infrastructure projects related to the 2022 hurricane.
cards.body:
FloridaCommerce announced it is distributing $7.2 million in Hurricane Ian Hazard Mitigation Grant Match Program grants to four municipalities still recovering from the Category 4 storm that made landfall near Fort Myers on Sept. 22, 2022, and then plowed through the peninsula. The FEMA funds are designed to provide infrastructure recovery, improve emergency preparedness and reduce the impact of future storms. Charlotte County will receive $5.83 million for erecting a public works hurricane-safe room generator, plus another $93,392 for a leachate waste plant generator project. The Port of the Islands Community Improvement District will get $750,840 for a Union Road water storage and infrastructure retrofit project. Seminole County has $319,437 in FEMA funds earmarked for a mitigation reconstruction project on Shad Lane, and the city of Palatka will receive $283,996 for a lift station generator.

Secretary of Commerce J. Alex Kelly said in a news release that thanks to Gov. Ron DeSantis' commitment to strengthening the state's long-term resiliency, Florida communities are getting the support they need to bolster critical infrastructure and storm-readiness. The Ian HMGMP program has already distributed more than $12 million in grants to municipalities in the wake of Hurricane Ian. The FEMA funding is provided on the condition the local governments will match the same amount of local money to complete the projects.

cards.headline: United States faces Belgium in World Cup Round of 16 with Florida fans watching
cards.teaser: The U.S. men's national team plays Belgium Monday night at Lumen Field in Seattle after earning the program's first knockout stage victory since 2002 against Bosnia and Herzegovina.
cards.body:
The United States men's national team takes the field Monday night against Belgium in the Round of 16 at Lumen Field in Seattle. The Americans earned the program's first knockout stage victory since 2002, having dispatched Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 on Wednesday night and playing the final 26 minutes plus stoppage time of that match with 10 men after Folarin Balogun was red-carded on what the American camp considered a maddening call. Longtime referee Andy Davies called the decision wrong, telling ESPN the contact was purely accidental and an unfortunate result from two players challenging for possession of the ball in a normal football movement. Coach Mauricio Pochettino said flatly it was never a red card, and the American camp was quick to note that Lionel Messi made a nearly identical challenge against Algeria earlier in the tournament and received nothing. Weston McKennie spoke for the locker room, saying the call was a bit bogus and adding that it is bogus.

Balogun, one of the team's top players, will watch Monday from the stands against a Belgian side that earned a Round of 16 win over the United States in the 2014 World Cup. Belgium has won six consecutive meetings against the U.S., including a 5-2 friendly rout in March, since the inaugural 1930 World Cup, the lone American victory in the head-to-head. The team is well-coached, physically capable, and playing at a venue where the home crowd will be as loud as any in the tournament.

cards.headline: European World Cup visitors face financial pressures from aging populations and high tax rates
cards.teaser: European fans traveling through the United States for the World Cup benefit from more vacation time than Americans, but face rising retirement ages and tax burdens at home as populations age.
cards.body:
Europeans traveling through the United States for the World Cup have more vacation time than most Americans, with European Union rules entitling workers to at least four weeks of paid annual leave. Many countries and collective agreements go beyond that minimum. The OECD's 2025 tax-wedge numbers show Belgium highest at 52.5% for a single average worker, followed by Germany at 49.3%, France at 47.2%, Austria at 47.1% and Italy at 45.8%. The OECD average was 35.1%. The tax wedge measures the gap between what it costs to employ a worker and what that worker takes home after income tax and social-security contributions.

On Jan. 1, 2025, 22% of the EU population was already 65 or older. Eurostat projects the working-age share of the EU population, those aged 20 to 64, to fall from 58% in 2025 to 50% by 2100. Germany's regular retirement age is already rising to 67 for Germans born in 1964 or later. A government-appointed pension commission has discussed a Swedish-style funded pension element, mandatory contributions and a gradual increase in the retirement age linked to life expectancy. Reuters reported that such a path could eventually push retirement toward 70. The United States faces Belgium next in the World Cup bracket, the only OECD country with a higher tax wedge than Germany.

cards.headline: Americans mark 250th anniversary with tempered enthusiasm about democracy's state
cards.teaser: In interviews across the country ahead of the Fourth of July, Americans expressed resilience and local focus rather than the brash confidence historically associated with the nation's image.
cards.body:
Americans celebrated the country's 250th birthday by tuning out partisan shouting from Washington and social media to focus on their own personal concepts of America. In Associated Press interviews with citizens in the days before the Fourth, auto technician Joe Fuqua-Bejarano in Topeka, Kansas, sized up what makes Americans awesome as resilience rather than politics. From the fireworks stand where he's doing a booming business as a side hustle, he said Americans have just got to find unity somewhere, whether that's in laughter or perseverance, and keep everybody cool.

Christina Zhou, a 25-year-old research assistant from Cambridge, Massachusetts, noted there are lots of points of contention going around, yet there are still a lot of beautiful things that are happening. She said she's trying to think about just things that are happening locally, which feels a little bit more like within personal control. In Mont Vernon, New Hampshire, farmer Mindy Dean, 50, and her family planned to milk their goats Saturday and maybe take in some local fireworks, though the 250th hoopla has been mostly lost on her. Neil Casey, an 81-year-old retiree from Nashua, New Hampshire, and his friend Maureen Regan from Cambridge roamed Boston's historical sites like Paul Revere's house and as many Fourth events as they could manage. Regan took heart in soccer fans who poured into the country for the World Cup and praised what they experienced, saying they love everything we have and advising compatriots to just enjoy the moment.

hero.headline: 40-year-old driver killed in head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
hero.body:
A 40-year-old man was killed early Sunday after a head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened around 2 a.m. near State Road 710, also known as Beeline Highway, and Southwest Silver Fox Lane.

FHP said a 2015 Kia Optima was traveling north on State Road 710 when the driver crossed into the southbound lane and collided head-on with a 2021 Toyota Tundra. The front left of the Kia struck the front left of the Tundra. Upon impact, the Kia burst into flames and came to rest on the grass shoulder facing north. The Tundra came to rest facing southeast in the southbound lane. The driver of the Kia, a 40-year-old man, died at the scene. The driver of the Tundra, a 41-year-old man from Indiantown, was taken to the hospital via LifeStar medical helicopter.

Martin County Fire Rescue has responded to 42 vehicle accident-related calls on State Road 710 just this year. After a fatal crash in January, Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek called the road a "death trap." Bill Townsend, who lives nearby, said the road has long been a concern for residents. "People don't pay a whole lot of attention to other people on the road, and [it's] kind of a dangerous road sometimes," Townsend said. "Everybody's always in a hurry… just living here makes me worry about the young people learning to drive and learning to drive on that road concerns me, because I have young kids."

The Florida Department of Transportation has plans to widen the road from two lanes to four, but construction is not expected to begin until 2031. "The question will be how many more people have to die before we get that project going. Florida touts that they have the safest roads in the country but this road is one that clearly is not in that category," Budensiek said in January. In the meantime, FDOT has begun improvements to the road, including pavement, markings, signage and new turn lanes. Townsend said faster action is needed. "It would be beneficial to the people that live and travel that road all the time if something happened faster," Townsend said.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation preserves Crain Estate history in Fort Pierce
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination while preserving the historic Crain Estate. The non-profit organization maintains the property once owned by Jaxson and Mary Crain, showcasing Mr. Crain's tile work throughout the facility. "Jackson is the one who did all the tiling throughout the facility, and you'll see it from the ground to the walls to the ceiling," says Krystal Masters, the art director. The foundation offers guided tours every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture.

The estate remains 90 percent unchanged from when the Crains lived there. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items including a gazebo shipped from India that features tiny peacocks on it. The smoking and bourbon room features man paneling and a bathroom with stained glass that leads to a bar on the front patio. Masters said the foundation made a conscious effort to preserve the estate's original character. "A lot of things we want to keep original. Yeah, we don't want it to be very commercialized," a foundation representative said.

The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, originally bringing in seven birds. The property now houses over 100 peacocks. A beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old, walks with a limp and is hand-fed daily from his own bowls. "Bob usually typically lives in here. He is a very spoiled peacock as you can see he has his own bowls we hand feed him everyday," says Masters. Tour guides say feeding the peacocks creates memorable moments with young visitors. The Crains also kept monkeys on the property. One story describes how Jackson Crain brought a baby monkey home from South America in his pocket.

The foundation operates an artist-in-residency program that attracts artists from around the world, providing simple but elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels. Masters leads one-on-one classes designed for complete beginners. "The majority of my classes are one on one classes you come in with zero experience and you walk out with a piece of art and it makes you feel good," Masters said. Classes cover various mediums including sculpting and watercolor. Masters views art as therapeutic. "Art is a form of therapy and it distresses people, leave happy and haven't been on their phone scrolling," she said.
